saints.name: St. Benedict
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: The father of Western monasticism, whose Rule of “pray and work” shaped the life of Europe for centuries…
biography: Born at Nursia in Umbria, Benedict withdrew as a young man to a cave at Subiaco to seek God, and gathered disciples into monasteries. At Monte Cassino he wrote his Rule, ordering the monastic day around prayer, sacred reading, and labor — ora et labora — with such discretion that it became the pattern of religious life throughout the West.
Through his monks the learning and faith of Christendom were preserved. He is honored as a patron of Europe.
saints.knownFor: Writing the Rule that founded Western monasticism.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; patron of Europe (1964)

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 11 July
